text.text_excerpt: I (finally!) stumbled upon Miss Linda at the Treme Gumbo Fest and I'm sure glad I did! It was love at first taste! This lady, and her family, serve up a slightly spicy and very hearty yakamein that will leave you wanting more. It's probably all the salt talking, but seriously... I look for Miss Linda "The Yakamein Lady" at every festival now. I'm partial to the beef, but there's usually a shrimp version offered as well. I've yet to see it on the menu, but per Lindsay A.'s high reccomendation, I will be waiting for a helping of Miss Linda's mac & cheese in the future. Oh, and since this seems to happen every time I'm in line... For the newbs out there: If you're wondering "What IS Yakamein...

Ms Linda's Yakamein is legendary! You must try it. It is so good. I only get to NOLA a few times a year and try to search out Ms Linda Green. I have been lucky enough to find her when she has other items available. Her Mac and cheese is fantastic too!

Miss Linda is getting all fancy (in her dress not in her food, don't worry) since winning Chopped in 2012. She had a custom chef's jacket with her name embroidered the last time I saw her. And because of her fame (see also: Bourdain's shows), she's being asked to cater a lot of different events. I don't see her at the Freret Market so much anymore, but that could change. I'm sure she'll be at Jazz Fest again this year, if you're hunting for her. Her food is soulful and delicious...but not very veggie friendly or for those who are watching their salt intake. She does have veggie yakamein at Jazz Fest usually and I love her mac-n-cheese. When she's done fried fish, that has been awesome too...
